channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: US youth vaping rate down 74% as scientist questions ‘epidemic’ label
item.description: A 74% fall in youth vaping changes the way the problem should be described. If use is declining sharply, the “epidemic” label may no longer reflect the evidence — and policy should adapt accordingly. Youth access still requires enforcement, but exaggerating the scale of the issue can distort public perception and justify restrictions that also harm adult smokers. Good public health depends on accurate labels, not outdated alarm. (Published on July 27, 2026byclearingtheair.eu)

item.title: Time to scrap the smoking ban
item.description: A smoking ban may look like a clean public health victory, but bans rarely stay simple once they meet real life. Adults who smoke are still adults, and policy has to balance harm reduction with autonomy, enforcement and unintended consequences. The better question is not how far restrictions can go, but whether they actually reduce smoking-related harm without pushing people into stigma, avoidance or less visible use. Public health should persuade, support and reduce risk — not rely on prohibition as its default language. (Published on July 27, 2026bythecritic.co.uk)

item.title: How Can Tobacco Harm Reduction Reach Marginalised Communities? #GFN26
item.description: Harm reduction cannot only reach the people easiest to reach. Marginalised communities often face the highest burden of smoking-related harm, while also having less access to trusted healthcare, stable support and practical quitting routes. Tobacco harm reduction has to be built with those realities in mind: affordable options, credible messengers and policies that do not add stigma to disadvantage. Reducing harm means reaching the people public health too often misses. (Published on July 28, 2026bygfn.tv)

item.title: Parliament discovers tobacco harm reduction
item.description: When parliament starts taking tobacco harm reduction seriously, the conversation changes. The focus can move beyond slogans about nicotine and towards the harder question of how to reduce smoking-related disease in practice. South Africa has an opportunity to build regulation that recognises the difference between combustible tobacco and lower-risk alternatives. Discovery is only the first step — the test is whether lawmakers turn evidence into proportionate policy. (Published on July 28, 2026bydailyfriend.co.za)
